lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing, Python
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Consider adding your current location.
items.because: It can help recruiters assess location or relocation fit.

items.says: Consider putting Experience before Education for product applications.
items.because: Leading with Education delays the reader from seeing your product experience.

items.says: Add a clear statement of your product-career direction and post-MBA transition near the top.
items.because: Your current Diesel Mechanic role makes your intended next step unclear.

items.says: The Harbor Payments internship has too many bullets for three months.
items.because: Some bullets overlap, so distinct outcomes and methods should take priority.

items.says: Clarify whether under five days per job is a typical result, maximum, or target.
items.because: It could be mistaken for an average or guarantee.

items.says: Clarify the scope or outcome of the hydraulic-systems and service-records work.
items.because: Its result is less clear than in the other bullets.

items.says: Clarify whether the time reduction was measured across all 2,300 merchants or a subset.
Clarify the A/B test’s scope and what shipping the flow to all merchants means.
items.because: The wording does not make clear whether the tested flow was rolled out after the experiment.

items.says: Explain how the RICE prioritization was used or what decision it informed.
items.because: The bullet only describes how Reach was defined and is less compelling than the outcome-focused bullets.

items.says: Shorten the process-heavy bullet and make the resulting roadmap priority more explicit.
items.because: The long After opening makes the key contribution arrive late.

items.says: Reduce the overlap with the checkout-conversion bullet.
items.because: The methodology should stay only if it demonstrates something important not apparent from the result bullet.

items.says: Distinguish the five-percentage-point conversion lift from a relative percentage change.
items.because: A change from 61% to 66% is five percentage points, not a 5% increase.

items.says: Clarify your role in securing funding and whether the additional regions launched or were only approved.
items.because: Funding is not the same as rollout.

items.says: Clarify your contribution and how the late-delivery reduction was measured.
items.because: The causal link to the scorecards is not fully established, and other factors may have contributed.

items.says: Add a verified baseline or time period for the pick-error reduction.
items.because: Neither is given.

items.says: Clarify your ownership relative to the supervisors and retrained pickers.
items.because: The current phrasing makes that relationship hard to parse.

items.says: Clarify the forecast-error definition or comparison period if needed.
items.because: That context may not be obvious to the audience.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the route-planning contributions and clarify your personal ownership.
items.because: The crowded bullet makes it difficult to tell which work drove the result.

items.says: Say whether the 1,800 driver hours are measured or estimated.
Clarify the measurement period for in its first year.
items.because: The project is still listed as ongoing.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students means eligible students or active users.
Growth from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: An incorrect calculation undermines trust in the other metrics.

items.says: Make the measurement period for the weekly-active-user figures clear.
State the pickup-slot increase as 20 percentage points rather than the ambiguous by 20%.
items.because: Moving from 75% to 95% is about 26.7% relative growth.

items.says: Clarify how the volunteer system produced or contributed to the fill-rate change.
Identify the $2.4M as a modeled or potential annual saving unless it was realized.
items.because: The client-funded pilot does not establish realized savings.

items.says: Replace the passive phrasing and identify your contribution.
items.because: The bullet does not make your role clear.

items.says: Clarify the impact of the intake-form changes if you have evidence.
items.because: The bullet gives no result beyond adoption.

items.says: Distinguish this pilot-approval bullet from the savings-model bullet.
items.because: Both describe the client-funded pilot and should show distinct contributions rather than repeat the outcome.

items.says: Clarify what you personally presented and distinguish pilot approval from realized results.
Organize the product skills into clearer, scan-friendly groups.
items.because: The list mixes methods, artifacts, and a programming language.

items.says: Consider listing SQL if you have used it.
items.because: It is absent and may matter for analytics-oriented product roles.

items.says: Make product analytics and design or engineering collaboration more visible if they reflect your experience.
items.because: The resume does not establish all of these role-dependent capabilities.
